en.name: NexusTransferPay
en.description:
NexusTransferPay is a cross-border money transfer app from American Group LLC. The transfer form, your balances and history, your credit score and an assistant sit behind one bottom bar, and the app is built around a single rule: it never shows you a number it did not get from the server.

SEND MONEY
Enter an amount, choose the currency you are sending from and the currency the recipient receives, then add the recipient's name, with an email address and a note if you want them. The form converts as you type, shows the exchange rate it used, and itemises the amount, the transfer fee and the total you will pay before you confirm. Ten currencies are supported: US dollar, euro, British pound, Mexican peso, Canadian dollar, Japanese yen, UAE dirham, Brazilian real, Indian rupee and Australian dollar.

NO INVENTED SUCCESS
A transfer is called successful only when the server returns a receipt that carries a reference and a status meaning accepted. A network failure, a timeout, an error, a missing reference, or a status the app does not recognise all end the same way: "Transfer failed", the reason, and "No money has been sent." There is no success screen for a transfer that did not happen. A receipt the server has accepted but not yet completed says "Transfer Submitted", and says plainly that delivery is not confirmed.

EXCHANGE RATES
Rates come from a public reference-rate feed. When that feed cannot be reached the app says the rate is unavailable and leaves the converted amount blank. It will not hand you a stale figure dressed up as today's rate.

DASHBOARD, HISTORY AND NOTIFICATIONS
Your wallet balances, with one tap to hide them, and your recent transactions. The history screen filters by sent, received or top-up and totals what you are looking at. Notifications are marked read only once the server confirms it. Every figure comes from your account on the server: when a call fails the screen shows a Service unavailable panel with a Retry button rather than a placeholder that looks like your money.

CREDIT SCORE
Your score and the factors behind it, drawn only from what the bureau returned. If a refresh does not actually complete, the gauge does not re-animate as though it did.

NOVA
Ask about a transfer, a rate or your figures in plain language. If the assistant cannot be reached the app tells you so in its own voice; it never puts words Nova did not produce into Nova's reply.

BORROW & PROTECT
Browse card, loan and insurance offers side by side, and size up a monthly payment with the loan calculator. In this version these screens compare only: Apply Now and Get Quote submit nothing, and the app says so on the spot instead of pretending an application is under way.

WHAT IT DOES NOT DO
NexusTransferPay is not a bank. It has no deposit account, pays no interest, and gives no financial advice. Card, loan and insurance applications cannot be submitted from the app. Premium pricing is shown on the Premium screen, but this version has no in-app purchase, takes no payment details and charges nothing. There are no ads. The app needs a network connection; anything it cannot load, it says it cannot load. Most of the interface is in English.

American Group LLC - www.safecodeg.com
Support: contact@safecodeg.com

review_information.notes:
2. DEVICES AND OS VERSIONS TESTED
Automated tests run on every build: iPhone 17 Pro Max and iPad Pro 13-inch simulators on iOS 26, and a Pixel Android emulator on API 34.
Each release is also installed and launched on those targets, so a
build that cannot start never ships.

3. WHAT THIS APP DOES, AND FOR WHOM
NexusTransferPay is a cross-border money transfer app from American Group LLC. The transfer form, your balances and history, your credit score and an assistant sit behind one bottom bar, and the app is built around a single rule: it never shows you a number it did not get from the server.

Intended audience:
General consumer audience; no specialist knowledge is assumed.

4. SETTING UP AND REACHING THE MAIN FEATURES
No account and no login are required. Every feature is reachable from the first screen after launch.

5. EXTERNAL SERVICES USED
- Apple In-App Purchase — paid features

6. REGIONAL DIFFERENCES
The app ships 25 languages (Arabic, Chinese (Simplified), English, French, German, Hindi, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish, bn, fa, fil, id, nl, pl, sv, ta, te, th, tr, ur, vi). Features are identical in every region.

7. REGULATED INDUSTRY OR THIRD-PARTY MATERIAL

The app is not in a regulated industry and carries no licensed third-party material. All content, artwork and copy are the developer's own.


ACCOUNT DELETION
The app creates no account, so there is nothing to delete.

_was_blocked_resolved.note: Failure paths, sign-out and the fabricated credit factors were fixed on 2026-09-15. Copy and the finance-category licensing/disclosure text must still come from the product owner, and nobody has confirmed the backend is reachable.

previous.no_copy_drafted: Copy deliberately not drafted — regulated category, unverified backend.
previous.evidence: Screens cover transfers, cards, loans, insurance, credit score and an AI chat (lib/screens/*). All of it runs against kBaseUrl = https://nexustransferpay.app (core/api_service.dart), which this sandbox cannot reach, so I cannot confirm a single transfer, loan or credit-score feature actually functions against a live backend. What has been confirmed is the failure behaviour: as of 2026-09-15 a transfer that does not come back with a receipt is reported as a failure and never as a success, and a release build shows a Service unavailable state rather than sample figures (test/transfer_failure_test.dart, 21 tests). Sign out now clears the stored session and leaves the signed-in shell, and the credit-score factor bars are drawn only from figures the bureau returned. Writing 'send money to anyone' for a money-transmission app whose backend I could not reach is still a claim I am not willing to make, and both stores apply extra scrutiny to the finance category.
previous.to_unblock: Copy must come from the product owner, together with the licensing and disclosure text both stores require for a financial-services listing.

  - Across all 43 apps the median pairwise similarity is 31%, and
    no pair exceeds 85%

Both numbers exclude the ~60 widgets every Flutter app uses — Column, Text,
Padding and so on. Including them makes any two Flutter apps look 97% alike,
which is a property of the framework rather than of these apps.

The store copy is distinct on the same basis: no two of the 43 share more
than 22% of their description vocabulary.
